content.p: Mamta Kafle Bhatt, a 28-year-old nurse who had emigrated from Nepal, has not been seen since the last days of July 2024. Her husband, Naresh Bhatt, is accused of killing her at their home in Manassas Park, Virginia, and of getting rid of her body. He has been held in jail since August 2024. Her body has never been found, but police and prosecutors say she is dead, and her blood was identified in the couple's house, according to Manassas Park Police Chief Mario Lugo.

Bhatt is charged with first-degree murder, defiling a dead body and concealing a dead body. These are allegations, not findings. No plea has been reported, and there is no verdict. A jury trial in Prince William County Circuit Court was set to begin with jury selection in the week of 5 October 2026, and was expected to run for about seven weeks.

Mamta Kafle Bhatt worked as a registered nurse in the medical-surgical unit of UVA Health Prince William Medical Center in Manassas, according to the hospital as told to CNN. Prosecutors said she usually worked two days a week. Police said she was last seen at the hospital on 27 July 2024. A surveillance camera caught her sitting outside the building with a friend that day, 7News reported. She called her friend Nadia Navarro the next day, 28 July, but Navarro was asleep and missed it. The same day Kafle Bhatt posted a last video on TikTok with her baby daughter, according to a WJLA report carried by CNN.

WTOP's 2026 coverage dates the last sighting differently, saying she was last seen by her mother in a video call on 29 July 2024. Prosecutors later told a judge that she habitually spoke to her mother twice a day, and that 29 July was the date of their final video call. She and her husband, who had been married for just over three years, had an 11-month-old daughter, Neema, who turned one on 20 August.

On 2 August, police went to the family's home after the hospital asked for a welfare check because she had missed work on 1 and 2 August without calling in. Bhatt told officers he did not want to report her missing. Prosecutors later said he told police she was visiting family in Texas or New York, and that she had no relatives in either state because her family lives in Nepal. He reported her missing three days later, police said. In a different account given in court, a prosecutor put that report on 6 August.

Between 5 and 8 August, detectives found that she had had almost no recent contact with relatives, friends, her employer or social media, and raised her status to involuntary or critical missing person. Police also said her credit cards, bank statements and phone showed no activity. Friends voiced confusion and questions about the timeline and how long it took to confirm she was missing. About 50 volunteers gathered at Blooms Park in Manassas one Thursday night in August to search on their own.
content.h2: Conflicting accounts of when she was last seen
content.p: The husband's own account changed in the reporting. Manassas Park police first said she was last seen on 31 July, which was what Bhatt had told them. After his arrest they gave 27 July, the last day she worked. CNN reported that Bhatt told investigators he last saw her at the dinner table on 31 July. A prosecutor said he first told police she was last seen in the early hours of 31 July and later said it was early on 1 August.

Bhatt gave interviews to news outlets. On 14 August 2024 he told WUSA he and his wife had eaten dinner together and "We do not have any argument or something like that," and said she had gone missing three times before, never for so long. Police said the public statements were not what he had told them, and Chief Lugo called some of them "misleading". Bhatt told FOX 5 in 2025 that he believed he was following police instructions when he waited before reporting her missing.

Detectives searched the house on 21 August 2024 and named Bhatt a person of interest; Lugo said he was not cooperating. Police arrested him the next morning at the house on a felony charge of concealing a dead body. The charge, NBC Washington noted, means police say they have evidence that a body was concealed, not necessarily that one was found. The couple's daughter was placed in the care of the Department of Social Services, and a 2025 report said she was being cared for by her family.

When Bhatt appeared in court on 23 August, prosecutors laid out their case in a criminal complaint. It said he murdered his wife "on or about" 30 July 2024. Investigators said that using BlueStar forensic technology they found what they believed to be blood in the main bedroom and bathroom. They described a bed pushed forward so that it blocked a closet, a pink stain on the carpet, and, after removing the bathtub, what they believed to be blood in its caulking. Prosecutors said digital and forensic evidence indicated her body had been inside the house and was dragged out. The complaint also said Mamta's phone kept receiving data until 29 July and had died by 1 August, with its last known location in Loudoun County. Bhatt said he had been at a cafe there and offered proof, which, prosecutors said, matched the last area where her phone contacted a tower.

His public defender argued that Bhatt had no criminal history and that the evidence did not support a class 6 felony. The judge denied his release. Bhatt's earlier service as a US Army Reserve logistics specialist from June 2017 to February 2024, without deployments, was confirmed by an Army spokeswoman.
content.h2: What prosecutors said at the bond hearing
content.p: On 20 September 2024 the court heard a longer account. Senior Assistant Commonwealth's Attorney Sarah Sami gave a timeline in a presentation of about 45 minutes, and said police had by then executed more than 25 search warrants. Among the allegations, all made by prosecutors and not tested at trial:

On the morning of 30 July, Bhatt took the couple's daughter to a babysitter's apartment in Manassas and was seen on camera putting bags into a dumpster there. He was seen discarding bags at several dumpsters on 30 and 31 July. Before dawn on 30 July he searched online for "Diagram of brain" and then "Chicken farm near me". He bought a set of knives at a Walmart and later a 40-pack of heavy black trash bags. At 1:30 a.m. on 31 July, he was filmed in Falls Church taking bags from his Tesla, and the car's tracking placed it there while his own phone was inactive. Sami also said the home used more than 150 gallons of water between 11 a.m. and noon on 31 July, against a typical 3 to 4 gallons an hour. A bathmat with light pink and reddish-brown staining that tested positive for blood was later found in a clothing donation bin, she said.

Sami argued that his sale of his Tesla and what she called a visible attempt to pack suitcases pointed to a plan to flee the country. At the August hearing, prosecutors had said a suitcase and passports for him and his daughter were visible in the house. She said Mamta missed her final immigration appointment to become a US citizen. She also said that in February 2024 Mamta had sent her brother in Nepal a photograph of her bloodied face and swollen eye "in case they needed to use it later." Judge Irving called the evidence as presented "overwhelming", at the level of probable cause, and denied bond. Holly Wirth, a former colleague of Mamta Kafle Bhatt and spokesperson for her family, said afterwards that, in her reading of the hearing, the family would not get Mamta back because of where the accused had put her remains, a reference to landfills.

Public defender Shalev Ben-Avraham told the court that Bhatt had served seven years honourably in the Army and would accept GPS monitoring. At an earlier pre-trial hearing the defence had said that she could still be alive and the case was at the stage of finding her. A judge ordered prosecutors to give the defence a surveillance video that appeared to show her getting into a black four-door sedan outside the hospital on 27 July.
content.h2: Murder charge and the evidence promised
content.p: On 2 December 2024 a grand jury indicted Bhatt for murder and physically defiling a dead body. At a press conference Chief Lugo said police had confirmed that blood found in the home was hers. "From the beginning, we believed that she was murdered," he said, and "I feel we have a strong case for not having the body." A search warrant executed while Bhatt was home with the couple's baby had found blood in the bedroom and bathroom, he said, and the evidence suggested dismemberment, which was the basis of the defiling charge. In court a prosecutor indicated that the amount of blood suggested injuries that were not survivable.

Later that month prosecutors gave notice that they would use Virginia Department of Forensic Science analysis. Four certificates, dated between 28 August and 12 November, covered DNA collected from several household items. The list included Mamta's hairbrush, carpet, a garbage can, a bathmat, a reciprocating saw and knives. John Fishwick, a defence lawyer giving 7News independent analysis, said the evidence put Bhatt in the house and linked blood on the saw to Mamta, although he expected the defence to challenge it. The defence objected to a prosecution plan to introduce Bhatt's broadcast news interviews as business records.

In August 2026 the prosecutors' witness subpoenas were reported to include forensic specialists, blood-spatter experts and mapping analysts, who prosecutors said would help the jury follow evidence tracking Bhatt's movements. WTOP reported that prosecutors have suggested he killed his wife at home, dismembered her with a power saw and put the remains in garbage bags left in dumpsters in the area. Defence lawyers had said in 2025 that they expected to face 24 prosecution experts.

The trial was first expected for September 2025. On 18 July 2025 Judge Irving, who called the request "mind-blowing", reluctantly granted a defence motion to postpone it to October 2026, saying that taking two years to prepare was surprising. Prosecutors Sami and Sweet had said they were ready, and did not object. Ben-Avraham cited about two terabytes of material from the prosecution; the written motion described more than 1.5 TB, including 1,626 items in one police case file and 2,561 in another, which it said took ten days to download. Bhatt told the judge he agreed to the delay. Mamta's family, through Wirth, said it was "profoundly disappointed" that the Commonwealth had not opposed it. A spokesperson for the prosecutor's office said they had confidence in their team.

In September 2026 the court was still working through the limits of the evidence. FOX 5 reported that the judge might admit two statements Mamta made about alleged domestic violence, while others would face hearsay objections, and that Bhatt's defence wanted all abuse allegations kept out. The proceedings would use four interpreters instead of the usual three, and the defence planned to ask for a delay in the start date. The judge ruled that there would be no live-streaming, citing protection of jurors' privacy and safety, with two pool cameras for delayed clips and still photographs allowed. Up to 300 prospective jurors were to be called to seat a jury and five alternates, and proceedings could stretch into November.

As of early October 2026 the reported schedule was that jury selection would start on 5 October (FOX 5) or 6 October (WTOP). A WTOP headline dated 7 October 2026 referred to the second day of the trial, polygraph evidence, witness lists and jury selection. The content of that report is not available here, and no plea or verdict has been reported. Bhatt has not been convicted. Chief Lugo has said that digital evidence has been crucial because her body has not been found. Supporters pledged in December 2024 to attend every day of the trial.
